new_statements.quote: Zhuang is a tone language. "While stress is assigned to multi-syllabic words in English, tone is assigned to monosyllable-based words or 'word-syllables' in Chinese". Like Chinese, word stress of Standard Zhuang is manifested by its tone. It has eight kinds of tone. [...] In the former, pattern of word stress is manifested by the tone consonant occurred at the end of the word. Hence, the stress symbol is overt. It is the word formation but not the stress of the word to determine the meaning of the word.
new_statements.citation: Liao, Zhi'en, Kavitha Ganesan & Jane Wong Kon Ling. 2024. Differences between English and the Zhuang Language in Phoneme and Word Stress. Higher Education and Practice (AEPH) 1(7): 1-7. doi:10.62381/H241701.
new_statements.locator: sec. 4.3 'Tone – Word Stress of Standard Zhuang', p. 3; sec. 5.2, p. 6; conclusion, p. 7
new_statements.reading: tone language with a stress statement
new_statements.check: confirmed by a second reader, with minor differences
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: The quotation was checked again., Higher Education and Practice 1(7) 2024). extracted text: sec. 4.3 'Tone – Word Stress of Standard Zhuang' begins bottom of p. 3: 'Zhuang is a tone language. "While stress is assigned to multi-syllabic words in English, tone is assigned to monosyllable-based words or 'word-syllables' in Chinese".[15] Like Chinese,' and continues at the top of p. 4: 'word stress of Standard Zhuang is manifested by its tone. It has eight kinds of tone. The first is ended with zero tone final, the second tone with the tone final "z", the third with "j"..'. Sec. 5.2 p. 6: 'In the former, pattern of word stress is manifested by the tone consonant occurred at the end of the word.…
new_statements.rule_in_words: The paper treats Standard (Wuming-based) Zhuang as having no word stress independent of tone: every syllable carries one of eight tones and 'stress' is simply the tone (written as a final tone letter). No syllable position is named. This is a pedagogical contrastive-analysis paper, not a phonological description; the genuine descriptions that could be opened (Coyaud 1987, Luo 2008, and everything in the ten daughter checks) say nothing about stress at all.
new_statements.domain_note: Standard Zhuang (Sawcuengh), the Wuming-based standard = Yongbei Zhuang [zyb] yong1276, one of the ten daughters of this retired node. Word level only; conflates stress with tone.
new_statements.identity_note: nort3249 is a retired ISO/Glottolog bookkeeping node ('Northern Zhuang' [ccx]), split in 2008 into ten languages: Guibian zgn (guib1244), Liujiang zlj (liuj1238), Qiubei zqe (qiub1238), Guibei zgb (guib1245), Youjiang zyj (youj1238), Central Hongshuihe zch (cent2009), Eastern Hongshuihe zeh (east2363), Liuqian zlq (liuq1235), Yongbei zyb (yong1276), Lianshan zln (lian1252). Any stress statement belongs to one of those daughters. The only work labelled ccx (Coyaud 1987) describes a Wuming-type variety (tone values 24 31 55 42 35 33) = Yongbei Zhuang [zyb] yong1276; the Liao et al. 2024 remark concerns Standard Zhuang, also Wuming/Yongbei-based; Luo 2008 describes Fengshan = Guibian [zgn] guib1244.

sources.note: Pedagogical contrastive paper on STANDARD (Wuming-based) Zhuang, not a linguistic description: sec. 4.3 p. 3 'Zhuang is a tone language.. Like Chinese, word stress of Standard Zhuang is manifested by its tone. It has eight kinds of tone.'; sec. 5.2 p. 6 'pattern of word stress is manifested by the tone consonant occurred at the end of the word. Hence, the stress symbol is overt.'; conclusion p. 7 'Word stress of the Standard Zhuang is manifested by tone'. Conflates stress with tone; no statement of stress position.
